concepts.def: The right amounts of carbohydrate, protein, lipid, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water.
Caused by too little or too much of one or more nutrients.
Breaking large insoluble food molecules into small soluble ones.
Caused by a lack of a nutrient, e.g. scurvy from too little vitamin C.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Nutrition & Health — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Nutrition & Health brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Nutrition & Health.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The enzyme that breaks down protein is:
options: protease
amylase
lipase
catalase

mcqs.q: Most absorption of digested food occurs in the:
options: small intestine
stomach
large intestine
mouth

mcqs.q: A lack of vitamin D in children can cause:
options: rickets
scurvy
anaemia
goitre

mcqs.q: Fibre is important in the diet because it:
options: helps move food through the gut and prevents constipation
provides most of the body's energy
is digested into amino acids
is absorbed to make bones strong
Bile digests proteins into amino acids.
Protease enzymes break proteins down into amino acids; amylase digests starch and lipase digests fats.
BMI measures how much sugar is in the blood.
Amylase digests proteins into amino acids.

mcqs.q: What is fibre's role if it isn't digested?
options: Bile digests proteins into amino acids.
Fibre adds bulk that helps muscles move food through the gut, preventing constipation, even though it isn't broken down.
Fibre is a nutrient that is digested for energy.
Fibre has no purpose because the body can't digest it.

mcqs.q: Does a high BMI always mean someone is unhealthy?
options: A high BMI always proves a person has too much body fat.
Fibre has no purpose because the body can't digest it.
BMI is only an indicator; a very muscular person can have a high BMI without excess fat, so it must be used with care.
BMI measures how much sugar is in the blood.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “BMI (body mass index)”?
options: A diet containing the right proportions of carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water for good health.
The movement of small, soluble products of digestion from the small intestine into the blood, mainly across the villi.
A nutrient needed to absorb calcium for healthy bones; a deficiency in children causes the bone disease rickets.
A value calculated from a person's mass and height that indicates whether they are underweight, a healthy weight or overweight.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Digestive enzyme”?
options: A biological catalyst that breaks large food molecules down; amylase digests starch, protease digests protein and lipase digests fats.
The movement of small, soluble products of digestion from the small intestine into the blood, mainly across the villi.
A value calculated from a person's mass and height that indicates whether they are underweight, a healthy weight or overweight.
A nutrient needed to absorb calcium for healthy bones; a deficiency in children causes the bone disease rickets.

sequence.def: Teeth chew; amylase begins starch digestion
Peristalsis pushes the bolus to the stomach
Enzymes finish digestion; nutrients absorbed by villi
Water absorbed from the remaining material
Faeces stored and egested through the anus
